subject: L1·L2·L3 weekly 2026-10-28: Capital and tech recycle into India; GaN buildout heats up

writer.headline: Capital and tech recycle into India; GaN buildout heats up
writer.intro: Biggest shift: domestic Indian listings are concentrating capital and recycling it into startups, especially AI and hardware plays. Western and Indian commitments to 300mm GaN fabs show heavy industrial capital flowing into semiconductor sovereignty. Investors are also backing AI-first preventive-health platforms in India. Energy-driven inflation and Israeli turnout trends rounded out the week's geopolitical pressures.

threads.line: Jio’s 21% IPO debut and a high listing valuation concentrated domestic capital, and that liquidity coincided with multiple early- and growth-stage raises into AI, hardware and consumer startups (examples include a $14M Series B with NVIDIA and Accel, Nova Spectral AI’s ₹21.2 Cr seed, and several pre-seed rounds).

Investors put fresh capital into AI-native preventive-health and radiology platforms, led by Cent’s $15M raise plus an acquisition and Live2.ai’s ₹130 Cr round supporting AI-enabled preventive and marketing-health plays.
Large-capital plans for 300mm GaN capacity advanced, with Infineon committing €1.1B to Europe’s first 300mm GaN fab and Spintronics planning a ₹2,800 crore fab in Madhya Pradesh.
Extremely high turnout—highest since 1981—and no clear majority increased signs of political fragmentation, with ~80% Arab turnout and record seat gains changing coalition math.
Oil-driven inflation showed up in producer prices—Malaysia PPI at 12%—and market chatter expects RBI intervention to support the rupee as oil pressures currency and capital flows.
Public political attacks on large corporations intensified, exemplified by Rahul Gandhi’s claim that Tata is being 'criminally destroyed', signalling elevated political pressure on major firms.

writer.watch: Watch whether Jio-era liquidity turns into larger, later-stage funds or M&A next week; also track any formal project approvals or financing for the 300mm GaN fabs, which would push the semiconductor thread from interest to industry buildout.
